objective: Give the deployed app a way to apply its schema. There is no production migration runner: alembic is a dependency and backend/alembic/ is real, but nothing in the deploy path ever runs 'alembic upgrade head', so a real deploy ships schema changes with no migration step. Add a migration handler and a Lambda that runs it on demand, sharing the existing image, invoked by a human and by nothing else.
acceptance_criteria: The synthesized Fanwire-App template contains a migration function whose code is the same DockerImageAsset the api function uses; the template contains no second image asset.
The migration function's image cmd override targets the migration handler, not app.main.handler.
Nothing in any synthesized template invokes the migration function automatically: it is the target of no EventBridge rule, no event source mapping, no Lambda schedule and no custom resource.
The migration function runs in the same VPC and app subnets and uses the same Lambda security group as the api function, so it can reach RDS.
The migration function's timeout is at least 300 seconds and its reserved concurrency is 1.
The IAM wildcard gate in infra/test/iam-policy.test.ts passes in all three domain modes, or any new wildcard is added to ALLOW_LIST with a written reason.
The migration handler runs alembic upgrade head programmatically against Settings.database_url and returns the head revision it arrived at.
A failed migration causes the handler to raise rather than return a success result, so an operator sees a failed invocation rather than a green one.
The handler does not log or return the database URL, its password, or any value derived from them.
